# Implement the client retry policy

The repository in `/app` holds `shipclient`, our HTTP client library. Engineering standards are published in the `docs` service, which you can use through the `docs` MCP server.

Implement `retry_delay` in `/app/shipclient/retry.py` so that it follows the current standards for retrying outbound HTTP requests: which failures and which requests are retried, how many attempts are made, how long to wait, and how `Retry-After` is handled, including the settings that differ per service. The docs service also holds superseded and draft versions of some standards; follow the ones in force.

Keep the function's signature and docstring contract, and use the Python standard library only. `/app/tests` has a few tests you can run with `cd /app && python -m unittest`; your implementation will also be checked against cases they do not cover.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

"""Retry policy for outbound HTTP calls made through shipclient."""

from datetime import datetime


def retry_delay(
    method: str,
    request_headers: dict[str, str],
    attempt: int,
    status: int | None,
    response_headers: dict[str, str],
    now: datetime,
) -> float | None:
    """Seconds to wait before the next attempt, or None to give up.

    `attempt` is the number of the attempt that just failed, 1 for the first.
    `status` is None when there was no response (a connection error).
    `now` is the current time, timezone-aware UTC.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError
import unittest
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from shipclient.retry import retry_delay

NOW = datetime(2026, 9, 16, 10, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


class RetryDelayTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_first_retry_of_a_get(self):
        self.assertEqual(retry_delay("GET", {}, 1, 503, {}, NOW), 0.25)

    def test_not_found_is_final(self):
        self.assertIsNone(retry_delay("GET", {}, 1, 404, {}, NOW))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
"}

{"server":"docs","tool":"mcp_docs_get_doc","result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"id\":\"http-client-standard-v3\",\"title\":\"HTTP client standard (v3)\",\"tags\":[\"api\",\"client\"],\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-04\",\"body\":\"# HTTP client standard (v3)\\n\\nStatus: current. Adopted 2026-08-04. Supersedes v2 (http-client-standard-v2).\\n\\nThis standard applies to every outbound HTTP call made through our client libraries.\\n\\n## When to retry\\n\\nA failed request is retried only when both of these hold:\\n\\n1. The failure is retryable: a connection error (no response at all), or a response with status 429, 502, 503 or 504. No other status is retried. In particular 500 is not retried, because our services return 500 only for bugs that a retry will not fix.\\n2. The request is safe to repeat: see the idempotency rules (doc idempotency-rules).\\n\\n## How many times\\n\\nBy default a request is attempted at most 5 times in total, counting the first attempt. After the last allowed attempt fails, give up.\\n\\n## How long to wait\\n\\nThe wait before the next attempt is exponential: 0.25 s after the 1st attempt, then doubling (0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s, ...), never more than the backoff cap, which is 8 s by default. The client library adds jitter in the transport layer; the delay function itself returns the exact value.\\n\\nFor 429 and 503 responses that carry a Retry-After header, see the rate limit rules (doc rate-limit-handling): they can make the wait longer, or stop the retries.\\n\\n## Retry profiles\\n\\nA request names the service it calls in the `X-Service` request header. A service can have a retry profile: a doc tagged `retry-profile` that sets three values for requests to that service: the attempt limit, the backoff cap, and the longest accepted Retry-After wait. These replace the defaults of this standard and of the rate limit rules. Everything else stays as stated here: which failures and which requests are retried, the 0.25 s first delay and the doubling.\\n\\nA service can have several profile docs (older revisions, proposals). Only a doc whose status line says it is current applies. A request without `X-Service`, or to a service that has no current profile, uses the defaults. Service names are matched exactly, ignoring case; header names are case-insensitive.\\n\"}"}]}}

{"server":"docs","tool":"mcp_docs_get_doc","result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"id\":\"rate-limit-handling\",\"title\":\"Rate limit handling\",\"tags\":[\"api\",\"client\"],\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-04\",\"body\":\"# Rate limit handling\\n\\nStatus: current.\\n\\nApplies to responses with status 429 or 503 that carry a Retry-After header. Other statuses ignore Retry-After.\\n\\nRetry-After holds either a number of seconds (an integer) or an HTTP date. For a date, the wait is the number of seconds from now until that date, and a date in the past means a wait of 0.\\n\\nAn HTTP date has exactly this layout: `Wed, 16 Sep 2026 10:00:05 GMT` (three-letter day name, comma, two-digit day, three-letter month name, four-digit year, 24-hour time, and the zone `GMT`). HTTP dates are always in GMT. A date with any other zone name or with a numeric offset is malformed, and so is a date in any other layout.\\n\\n- If the Retry-After wait is more than the longest accepted wait, 30 seconds unless the service's retry profile sets another value, do not retry at all.\\n- Otherwise wait whichever is longer: the Retry-After wait or the exponential delay from the HTTP client standard. The backoff cap does not apply to the Retry-After wait.\\n- A malformed Retry-After value is ignored, as if the header were absent.\\n\\nHeader names are case-insensitive.\\n\"}"}]}}

I implemented `retry_delay` in `/app/shipclient/retry.py` and wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`. `python -m unittest` passes (2 tests, OK). A few spot checks of my own also gave the results I expected. I didn't write more tests beyond that.

The rules come from the in-force docs (HTTP client standard v3, rate limit handling, idempotency rules):
- **Which failures:** connection errors and status 429, 502, 503 and 504. 500 and everything else is final.
- **Which requests:** GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT and DELETE are retried. POST and PATCH are retried only with a non-empty `Idempotency-Key`. Method names and header names are case-insensitive.
- **Attempts and delay:** the default is 5 attempts in total. The wait is 0.25 s, doubling each time, capped at 8 s.
- **Retry-After:** it applies only to 429 and 503.
  - The value is either integer seconds or a strict `GMT` HTTP date. A date in the past means a wait of 0.
  - A malformed value is ignored.
  - If the wait is over the longest accepted wait (30 s by default), the function gives up.
  - Otherwise the delay is the longer of the Retry-After wait and the backoff, and the backoff cap doesn't apply to the Retry-After wait.
- **Per-service settings:** `X-Service` is matched ignoring case. These services have a current profile: catalog, ledger, auth, payments, ledger-export, reports, inventory, search, shipping and media. I ignored the draft, superseded and withdrawn profile docs, including the v4 draft, the shipping draft, the geo profile (withdrawn) and the notify profile (draft). Services with no current profile get the defaults.

Two cases the docs don't spell out, where I made a call:
- An HTTP date whose weekday doesn't match the date is accepted. Only the layout and a real calendar date are checked.
- A whitespace-only `Idempotency-Key` counts as empty.
